title: 2025-05-21 NovaTech QBR - usage & roadmap
summary: Quarterly health check covering usage trends, cost drivers, recent reliability incidents, upcoming roadmap alignment, and next steps for a pilot scale-up. Action items include a cost breakdown, 24-hr load test, and security docs share.
action_items: Luis Ortega: Send detailed cost breakdown by model & route (due 2025-05-26)
Ravi Patel: Run 24-hour load test on staging cluster and share results (due 2025-05-28)
Maya Chen: Share SOC2 and KMS integration docs; intro to solutions engineer for VPC options (due 2025-05-23)
Marcus Li: Provide sample retention and PII use-cases for compliance review (due 2025-05-30)
next_steps: Redwood to send pricing spreadsheet and historical usage delta analysis
Start pilot for Dedicated pool if benchmarks meet latency SLOs
Customer to confirm compliance stakeholders for private deployment convo
transcript:
15:00 Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining the QBR. We scheduled 50 minutes - we can run a little over - main goals: usage/cost review, a quick look at the April incidents, and then roadmap alignment and next steps.
15:12 Ellen (NovaTech CTO): Thanks Maya, appreciate it. We're coming off a spike in transactions during seasonal promotion and wanted to understand cost implications and whether Dedicated makes sense.
15:20 Marcus (Platform Lead): Quick context - production is about 120 req/s peak, average is around 25 req/s, embeddings at about 10k calls/day. We're seeing tail latency higher than expected on long-context chats.
15:33 Luis (Redwood CSM): Got it. We'll go through the cost breakdown first. Maya, do you want to start?
15:38 Maya (Redwood AE): Sure. On the cost side the big drivers were: more long-context chat sessions hitting >4k tokens, and a handful of rerank/embedding-heavy routes. We noticed two model variants in the same route - mixed quantization - that bumped unit cost. We'll send a route-level spreadsheet after.
15:55 Ellen: When you say mixed quantization, does that mean we can optimize without accuracy loss? We've had some concerns about hallucination variance when moving to 4-bit.
16:03 Ravi (Redwood SE): Yeah, quick note: quantization profiles are model and workload dependent. For the chat routes with long contexts we recommend maintaining fp16 for the central model and trying 4-bit only for embeddings or batch offline tasks. There can be perf regressions in some generation patterns.
16:18 Sasha (SRE): We also recorded two minor incidents in April - one was a routing mismatch during the East region maintenance window that caused failover delays (~4 minutes), second was KV cache eviction causing token regen for 12% of requests for a 30-minute window.
16:31 Luis: Thanks Sasha. On the failover event we flagged automatic fallback policy change - Redwood logs show automatic fallback occurred but there was a delayed DNS update which increased latency. We've raised a ticket and SE is proposing a pre-warm strategy for the standby pool.
16:45 Marcus: Pre-warm sounds good. Can you quantify cost delta for pre-warm vs current cold starts?
16:52 Maya: Initial estimate: pre-warm adds about 8-12% to committed GPU minutes but reduces tail latency by 40-60% depending on workload. We'll provide precise numbers for your current traffic profile.
17:05 Ellen: Another ask - we need audit logs and KMS key rotation compliance. We've been asked by InfoSec whether Redwood supports customer-managed keys and 7-year audit retention.
17:14 Maya: Yes, Redwood supports KMS integration and long-term logs via the enterprise add-on. I'll share SOC2 artifacts and the KMS integration guide. For retention beyond standard retention we'll engage the compliance team, but it's supported as an add-on.
17:28 Jared (Product): Roadmap question: we want more deterministic control over routing by user tier so we can pin high-value users to Dedicated capacity. Is that on your roadmap?
17:36 Ravi: Short answer: yes. We have policy-based routing that's currently config-driven for beta customers; full per-tenant pinning and route affinity is slated for the next quarter. We can offer a canary today by using route tags and explicit routing rules.
17:48 Ellen: Latency SLOs - our bar is 200ms p50 for short queries and <700ms p95 for longer chats. Can you meet that with hosted or do we need Dedicated?
17:58 Ravi: For your current mix, hosted can hit p50 ~180ms for short queries but p95 creeps over 700ms under peak. Dedicated with pre-warm and optimized batching typically brings p95 down to ~400-500ms in our benchmarks. We'll run a mirror test to be sure.
18:13 Marcus: What about autoscaling - we can't commit to a large reserved pool yet, want burst options.
18:20 Maya: Redwood Dedicated supports committed capacity + burst to shared capacity. We can model expected burst costs; that's in the spreadsheet we'll send.
18:30 Ellen: Are there any compatibility issues if we go private/VPC later? We might want to move sensitive workloads on-prem in 2026.
18:38 Ravi: Private deployment is supported; we do a separate control plane and customer-managed networking. There are additional operational requirements - storage for KV cache locality and network egress considerations. We have a migration checklist we can share.
18:52 Luis: Ok next, quick demo snippet - Ravi, could you show the error/latency traces you mentioned?
18:56 Ravi: Sure, sharing my screen - sorry folks if names are a bit off, the auto-transcription sometimes messes them up. (screen) Here is the tail latency chart for last 30 days; circled area is April 12 where we saw the eviction pattern. You can see the p95 spike aligns with heavy embedding jobs at midnight. The KV eviction correlates with lower memory thresholds on that cluster.
19:18 Sasha: We run nightly batch job for embeddings - can that be throttled or moved to dedicated lower-priority nodes?
19:24 Ravi: Yes, options: throttling, scheduled windows, or shifting to a separate embedding-optimized instance which is cost-effective. That would reduce contention for KV cache.
19:36 Ellen: Good. On compliance, who is the Redwood point-of-contact for legal/security? We need an NDA addendum for HIPAA scoping.
19:45 Maya: I'll introduce you to our security lead, Priya Nair, and send the SOC2 pack plus HIPAA scoping questionnaire.
19:52 Marcus: Any blockers for running the 24-hour load test on staging? We want to validate p95 during prolonged peak.
19:58 Ravi: No blockers. We'll need a staging key and traffic template - Luis can coordinate. We'll run an identical routing policy and quantization profile. Expect results within 48 hours after start.
20:12 Ellen: Ok thanks. Summarizing: Redwood to send cost and route-level breakdown, SE runs 24-hour test, share SOC2/KMS docs, and we reconvene after bench to decide on Dedicated pilot.
20:22 Maya: Perfect. I'll follow up with the spreadsheet and schedule the bench for next week. Any final questions?
20:28 Jared: One last ask - can you include a sample SLA for Dedicated? We want hard numbers on uptime and support response times.
20:34 Maya: Yup - will include SLA PDF and the Dedicated spec sheet.
20:40 Ellen: Great, thanks everyone.
20:42 Luis: Thanks all - action items will be in the follow-up email.
20:45 meeting ended
